messages:
sara: quick check — RFC followup: we need a concrete eligibility matrix for gateway-level fallbacks. putting notes here for triage.
ajay: can we scope this to three axes? model-tier (prod/canary/dev), latency-sla, and safety-score threshold.
taylor: yes, and add 'last-successful-kernel' as a fourth axis so we don't flip between incompatible caches.
eli: are we planning per-model persisted flags or per-model-version? persisted flags sound heavy.
sara: prefer per-model-version where possible. fallback eligibility should be evaluated at request time with rules stored in config service.
ajay: +1. runtime should evaluate: if model.version != pinned && safety_score < X -> route to fallback-kernel.
ops-bot: NOTICE: scheduled deploy window 03/22 02:00-04:00 UTC for gateway-config service.
taylor: ops-bot noted. we should avoid any config schema changes during that window.
eli: what about a manual override for emergent safety regressions? product asked for an escape hatch.
sara: include an emergency 'circuit_breaker' flag at gateway-level that forces all requests for that model-id to go to safe-kernel. admin-only toggle with audit log.
ajay: audit log + MFA for that toggle? Security wants a second approver.
taylor: MFA + approver sounds good. also add an automatic cooldown: if circuit_breaker enabled, block re-enable for 10m without approval.
eli: telemetry: need counters for eligibility decisions: why we chose fallback (latency|safety|quota|kernel_mismatch). and histograms of time-to-fallback decision.
sara: add spans for evaluation path. send to console traces tag=eligibility-eval.
ajay: sample config snippet we discussed: ```json
{"model_tiers": ["prod","canary","dev"], "rules": [{"match": {"tier":"prod","safety_below": 0.7}, "action": "fallback:kernel-safe-v1"}, {"match": {"last_successful_kernel":"kv-cache-v2","latency_above_ms":120}, "action":"fallback:stateless-small"}] }
```
taylor: looks good. small nit: use explicit action types so we can support A/B rollouts (action.type = redirect|mirror|fallback).
eli: how do we prevent thrashing? if eligibility flips frequently, we could be moving traffic every minute.
sara: introduce hysteresis windows per-rule (min_duration and cool_down). example: enable fallback after 3 consecutive eval failures, remain for 5m.
ajay: and telemetry alert when a rule causes >20% traffic shift in 10m.
ops-bot: ALERT: gateway-config feature flag updated by deploy-bot (sara) — change will be staged in canary.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: gateway-config v2.3.7 -> canary (5% traffic).
taylor: confirm canary includes eligibility eval tracing. eli, can you watch for false positives on safety-driven fallbacks?
eli: on it. I'll create an eval dashboard showing fallback reasons + sample requests.
sara: followups: 1) finalize schema with security, 2) wire admin override + MFA, 3) add telemetry spans + alerts, 4) plan controlled canary. assign owners?
ajay: I'll take schema + hysteresis logic.
taylor: I'll own canary plan and rollout playbook.
eli: I'll do telemetry dashboard and sampling hook.
sara: cool. post-RFC tracker: add a checklist entry and ping infra for KMS access for audit logs.
ajay: quick question — for models pinned to dedicated hardware, do we bypass gateway fallbacks?
sara: no, still evaluate, but default action is 'fallback to local-compatible variant' rather than cross-region kernel. document that.
taylor: noted. I'll add a row in the canary runbook for 'pinned model behavior'.
eli: one more: rate-limit interactions between fallback and batching. if fallback reduces batch size, we should surface cost delta in console.
sara: add to Optimize team asks. mentioning @product-lead in the doc.
ajay: ok, created a short PR draft for the schema. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/gateway-config/pull/482
taylor: will review in morning. good progress. :thumbsup:
